subject: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal

Hi team,

Following our Q3 hiring review I put together a short proposal for how we should handle remote, geo-specific adjustments for offers across US / EU / APAC. Key constraints: keep our band structure intact, maintain equity between similarly leveled ICs, and avoid creating manual exceptions at scale.

Attached: regional_col_adjust_v2.xlsx (tabbed by role family + recommended percent adjustments relative to US benchmark).

High-level options I modeled:
- Option A: Market parity — convert to local market medians (high admin overhead).
- Option B: Band-floor + COLA delta — keep Redwood band but apply location multiplier (simpler).
- Option C: Role-tier uplift — only adjust for junior/senior tiers in high-cost/low-cost regions.

Quick asks: can HR review preferred option and give a recommended delta schedule for EU cores (DE/FR/NL/IE) and APAC hubs (IN, SG, AU)? Also need guidance on whether we treat compensation as total cash vs. base-only in candidate-facing language.

Thanks — I want to pilot something for offers that go out in early Oct.

— Marcus
Sr. Dir, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: regional_col_adjust_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 220KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal

Thanks Marcus — good framing. A few initial thoughts before HR takes a deeper pass: 

1) Communication: candidate-facing offers should present a single "total cash" figure and a short footnote: "Offer adjusted for local market norms". Avoid exposing multipliers.

2) Approval gates: any offer using >10% location uplift vs. band midpoint requires Director-level approval (Vivek).

3) Equity/stock: keep equity buckets equal across locations for the same level; we can adjust grant cadence if needed.

Laura — can you run two scenarios and share a redline to the offer template?
Vivek — please confirm if you're comfortable with the 10% gate or if we should set a different threshold for contractors vs full-time.

Neha
VP, Talent & Org Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Offers Ops <offers@talentops.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 5:03 PM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — good framing. A few initial thoughts before HR takes a deeper pass: 

Team — I reviewed Marcus's workbook and added a "Recommended" tab with concrete percent adjustments (rounded) and a short rationale. Summary:
- EU core hubs (DE/FR/NL/IE): -2% to +4% relative to US band midpoints (varies by role family).
- UK: +6% relative to US midpoint for senior technical ICs (market premium).
- India (Bengaluru): -35% to -20% depending on level; Singapore: -8% to -2%; Australia: -2% to +2%.

Proposal for rollout:
- Pilot: hires submitted between Oct 1 - Dec 31. Apply Band-floor + COLA delta (Option B).
- Approval flow: Recruiter -> Hiring Manager -> HR (Laura) -> Director (Vivek) for >10% uplift.
- Offer language: share total cash and a short parenthetical: "Compensation is adjusted for local market norms."

I've attached an updated offer template with bracketed fields for location.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal

Thanks Laura — that level of granularity is helpful. I approve running Option B as a pilot for Q4 with the approval gates you outlined. A few clarifying points: 

- Cap the maximum uplift we will approve in pilot at +20% for any single hire unless the headcount owner makes a business case to Execs.
- Contractors: treat separately; contractor pay should be set by ops/finance (we will default to local market unless exception requested).
- Legal: coordinate with contracts to ensure offers remain compliant for cross-border tax withholding and statutory benefits disclosures.

Let's finalize offer template language and a short manager FAQ (2 pages) that recruiters can use. Marcus — please share the candidate list you expect to be impacted in Oct so we can pre-approve where possible.

Vivek
COO, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Müller <sofia.muller@larkspur.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remote offers: geo differentials and COLA proposal

Hi Neha / Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the update. We have a candidate (Backend Engineer, Level IC3) based in Berlin for Larkspur Technologies who received a verbal offer based on US benchmark numbers. Before we issue the written offer, can you confirm: 

1) Will the EU recommended delta be applied to the total cash offer or base-only?
2) If we apply Laura's recommended -2% to +4% band, should we round to nearest €500?

We're attaching the candidate brief and suggested numbers — if it's quicker to approve them directly I can share the candidate ID.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Recruiter, Larkspur Technologies
Attachment: candidate_brief_berlin_candidate123.pdf (pdf, 95KB)
